# Pages

## `Page`

```python
Page(document: Document, number: int, generation: int)
```

A page of a document, named by its page object.

A page stays the same page when other pages are inserted, moved, or
deleted; `index` follows it. Once the page itself is deleted, its
reads raise `StalePageError`, and they work again if undo
restores it. Two pages are equal when they name the same page object of
the same document.

### `Page.document`

```python
Page.document: Document
```

The document that holds the page.

### `Page.xref`

```python
Page.xref: int
```

The object number of the page dictionary.

```python
Page.obj: Dictionary
```

The page dictionary as a handle of the low-level object model.

Page.annotations: Annotations
```

The page's annotations other than links and form widgets, in `/Annots` order.

Page.links: Links
```

The page's link annotations, in `/Annots` order.

### `Page.images`

```python
Page.images(*, annotations: bool = True) -> list[PageImage]
```

Return the images that the page paints, in the paint order of `content`.

Each `PageImage` decodes its pixels with `pixmap()` and
returns its data as stored with `stored()`; `annotations` counts
the images of annotation appearances, as in `content`.

### `Page.fonts`

```python
Page.fonts() -> list[FontInfo]
```

Return the fonts that the page's resources and its Form XObjects' resources name, one per font dictionary.

The resources are the page's own or those it inherits from the page
tree; Form XObjects are followed through their `/Resources` to any
depth, each once. Fonts that only annotation appearances or Type 3
glyph procedures name are not listed. A page tree deeper than 64
parents, more than 4096 forms, or more than 65536 font and XObject
entries over the walk raise `LimitError`.
`Document.font_program` returns a font's embedded program.

### `Page.label`

```python
Page.label: str
```

The page's label from `doc.page_labels`, or `""` when no range covers it.

### `Page.rotation`

```python
Page.rotation: int
```

The page's `/Rotate`, inherited and normalized to 0, 90, 180, or 270.

Assigning a multiple of 90 sets the page's own `/Rotate`, in one
transaction; another value raises `ValueError`.

Settable.

### `Page.rect`

```python
Page.rect: Rect
```

The display `Rect` `(0, 0, width, height)`, with the rotation applied.

The visible page is the CropBox clipped to the MediaBox; a box that
leaves nothing visible gives the A4 page that the renderer draws.

### `Page.media_box`

```python
Page.media_box: Rect
```

The page's MediaBox in display space, inherited, or the A4 page that the renderer draws.

Display space is the visible page's, with `(0, 0)` at its top-left,
so a MediaBox larger than the CropBox has negative coordinates.
Assigning a `Rect` in the same space sets the page's own
`/MediaBox` in one transaction. A MediaBox that would not hold a
box the page sets raises `ValueError`; set that box first.

Settable.

### `Page.crop_box`

```python
Page.crop_box: Rect
```

The page's CropBox in display space: inherited, clipped to the MediaBox, and the MediaBox when absent.

Assigning a `Rect` in the current display space sets the
page's own `/CropBox` in one transaction, and the visible page,
the renderer, and text coordinates follow it. A box that leaves the
MediaBox raises `ValueError`.

Settable.

### `Page.bleed_box`

```python
Page.bleed_box: Rect
```

The page's BleedBox in display space, clipped to the MediaBox, and the CropBox when absent.

Assigning a `Rect` in the current display space sets the
page's own `/BleedBox` in one transaction; a box that leaves the
MediaBox raises `ValueError`.

Settable.

The page's TrimBox in display space, clipped to the MediaBox, and the CropBox when absent.

Assigning a `Rect` in the current display space sets the

The page's ArtBox in display space, clipped to the MediaBox, and the CropBox when absent.

Assigning a `Rect` in the current display space sets the

Settable.

### `Page.pixmap`

```python
Page.pixmap(
    *,
    dpi: float | None = None,
    matrix: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    alpha: bool = False,
    background: tuple[int, int, int] | tuple[int, int, int, int] | None = None,
    annotations: bool = True,
    colorspace: Colorspace | Literal['gray', 'rgb'] = <Colorspace.RGB: 'rgb'>,
) -> Pixmap
```

Render the current version of the page to a `Pixmap`.

`dpi` scales the page uniformly, 72 by default; `matrix` is a
`Matrix` or six entries, whose translation is dropped, since
the raster covers the transformed page, or a linear map
`(a, b, c, d)`. Without `alpha` the page lies on white.
`background` is an RGB or RGBA tuple with components from 0 to 255
painted beneath the page, which must be opaque without `alpha`.
`annotations=False` leaves out the appearances of annotations and
form widgets. `colorspace="gray"` converts the rendered colors to
gray with ITU-R BT.601 luma weights.

`clip` is a display rectangle `(x0, y0, x1, y1)`: its bounding
box under the matrix, rounded outward to whole pixels and
intersected with the page, is all that is rasterized. A clip that
leaves no pixel of the page raises `PdfError`, and the size
limits of the whole page still apply: a raster is at most 65,408
pixels wide, 65,532 high, and 64,000,000 in all, and a larger one
raises `ValueError`. The GIL is released while hayro renders.

### `Page.draw`

```python
Page.draw(*, underlay: bool = False) -> Canvas
```

Return a `Canvas` that draws on this page when its `with` block ends.

The drawing is one transaction and one undo step, painted over the
page's content or, with `underlay=True`, beneath it.

### `Page.replace_text`

```python
Page.replace_text(old: str, new: str, *, count: int | None = None) -> int
```

Replace `old` with `new` where simple fonts draw it, and return the number of replacements.

`old` is found in the strings of each text-showing operation of
the page's content and of the Form XObjects that it draws, decoded
through the operation's Type 1, TrueType, or Type 3 font as text
extraction reads it, across the strings and kerning of a `TJ`
array but not across operations. `new` is encoded through the
same font, and a kerning number after it makes up the difference in
advance, so the text that follows keeps its position. A Form
XObject's text is read with the text state where it is drawn.
`count` bounds the replacements, in drawing order; `None`
replaces all.

A character of `new` that the font has no code for, and `old`
drawn in a composite (Type 0) font of the page's content, raise
`ValueError` and leave the document unchanged. Form XObjects
nested deeper than 16, or more than 4,096 drawings of them, raise
`LimitError`. A font subset is not extended, so a code
without a glyph in the program shows as the program's missing glyph.
A drawing of a Form XObject that changes draws a copy, so the other
drawings, pages, and Forms that share it keep the old text. The
replacement is one transaction.

### `Page.flatten`

```python
Page.flatten(*, annotations: bool = True, widgets: bool = True)
```

Draw this page's annotation and widget appearances into its content and take them off.

As `Document.flatten` does for one page, except that the
widgets leave their fields, and a field leaves the form with its
last widget, rather than the form leaving the document.

### `Page.ocr`

```python
Page.ocr(
    *,
    engine: OcrEngine | None = None,
    dpi: float = 300,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    rotation: OcrRotation = 0,
    tile_size: int = 1408,
    overlap: int = 192,
    min_confidence: float = 0.5,
) -> list[OcrWord]
```

Recognize the rendered page's text without changing the document.

The default engine is loaded lazily from `pyropdf[ocr]` and reused.
Pass an explicit `OcrEngine` to control the model set or its
lifetime. `clip` recognizes one display-space region and returns
boxes in full-page display space. `rotation` corrects sideways input
clockwise without editing the page.

### `Page.apply_ocr`

```python
Page.apply_ocr(
    *,
    words: Iterable[OcrWord] | None = None,
    engine: OcrEngine | None = None,
    dpi: float = 300,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    rotation: OcrRotation = 0,
    skip_existing: bool = True,
    tile_size: int = 1408,
    overlap: int = 192,
    min_confidence: float = 0.5,
) -> list[OcrWord]
```

Add an invisible, searchable text layer and return the words it holds.

Without `words`, the page is recognized as `ocr` recognizes it.
`words` takes the `OcrWord` records that another engine, such
as Tesseract or a cloud service, recognized, with boxes in display
space; the recognition options do not apply to them. The text is not
drawn and appears only in extraction and search. An Identity-H
reference font with ToUnicode is used without embedding font data, so
any language, including CJK, adds almost no file size. One call takes
at most 4,096 words with text and 1 MiB of UTF-8 text, and adds the
layer in one transaction.

By default, a page with extractable text is skipped, which makes
repeated calls idempotent and avoids duplicate text layers; with
`clip`, only text that meets the region counts. Use
`skip_existing=False` to add the layer anyway; existing text is kept.
`rotation` is the clockwise correction that reads sideways input and
orients the invisible baselines. An empty result changes nothing.

### `Page.svg`

```python
Page.svg(*, annotations: bool = True, max_size: int | None = 67108864) -> str
```

Render the current version of the page to an SVG string at 72 dpi, with text drawn as paths.

`annotations=False` leaves out the appearances of annotations and
form widgets. `max_size` caps the UTF-8 output and defaults to
64 MiB, raising `LimitError` with code `svg_output_size`;
`None` opts out. hayro-svg builds its whole string before the limit
is checked, so the limit keeps an oversized result from becoming a
Python string rather than bounding the converter's memory. The GIL
is released while hayro-svg converts.

### `Page.content`

```python
Page.content(
    *,
    text_runs: bool = True,
    paths: bool = True,
    images: bool = True,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    annotations: bool = True,
    max_elements: int | None = 262144,
) -> Content
```

Return the text runs, paths, and images that the page paints.

Items come in paint order, in display coordinates, as hayro
interprets the current version of the page, with optional-content
visibility applied. Each carries its paints, its blend mode and soft
mask, and the `GraphicsContext` of clips, transparency groups,
and marked content that encloses it. Glyph boxes are the exact boxes
of the glyph outlines. hayro paints every image inside a transparency
group that holds the graphics state's opacity, blend mode, and soft
mask, so an image's context ends with that group. A shading painted
with `sh` is a `Path` that covers the clip region and fills
with a `ShadingPattern`.

`text_runs=False`, `paths=False`, and `images=False` leave out
that kind of item without building it. `clip` keeps the items whose
box meets a display-coordinate rectangle. `annotations=False` leaves
out annotation appearances, which otherwise follow the page content.
Items whose geometry or paint is not finite, which hayro cannot paint
either, are left out.

`max_elements` bounds the glyphs, path and clip segments, stroke
dash lengths, and items of one interpretation, before `clip`
applies; above it the call raises `LimitError` with code
`content_element_count`. `None` removes the bound for trusted
input. The GIL is released while hayro interprets the page.

### `Page.text`

```python
Page.text(
    *,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    clipped: bool = False,
    ligatures: bool = True,
    whitespace: bool = True,
    dehyphenate: bool = False,
    unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip',
    max_glyphs: int | None = 262144,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> str
```

Return the text of the current version of the page in reading order.

Reading order follows the geometry and script heuristics described in
the documentation rather than the document's semantic order. Spaces
between words are inferred from glyph positions, and lines end with a
newline. Annotation appearances count as page content.

`clip` keeps the glyphs whose box's center lies inside a
display-space rectangle, in the page's reading order, which gives the
text in a rectangle. Glyphs that the page boundary or the clip paths
hide entirely are left out unless `clipped=True`; invisible text,
such as an OCR layer, is kept. `ligatures=False` expands the
ligature characters U+FB00 to U+FB06 to their letters;
`whitespace=False` makes every whitespace character a space;
`dehyphenate=True` removes a hyphen that ends a line between two
letters of a word that continues in lowercase on the next line of the
block, and joins the two lines; and `unmapped` decides what a glyph
without Unicode becomes (see `Unmapped`).

`max_glyphs` bounds the glyphs collected, 262,144 by default, with
`LimitError` code `text_glyph_count`, and `max_size` the
UTF-8 of their text and of the returned text, 64 MiB by default, with
code `text_size`; `None` lifts either. The GIL is released while
hayro interprets the page.

### `Page.words`

```python
Page.words(
    *,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    clipped: bool = False,
    ligatures: bool = True,
    whitespace: bool = True,
    dehyphenate: bool = False,
    unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip',
    exact_bboxes: bool = False,
    max_glyphs: int | None = 262144,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> list[Word]
```

Return the words of the current version of the page in reading order, as `Word` records.

Boxes are in display space and span the glyphs' advances and the
font's ascender and descender, or their outlines with
`exact_bboxes=True`. The other options are those of `text`; a
word that dehyphenation joins is one `Word` on its first line
whose box spans both parts.

### `Page.layout`

```python
Page.layout(
    *,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    chars: bool = False,
    clipped: bool = False,
    ligatures: bool = True,
    whitespace: bool = True,
    dehyphenate: bool = False,
    unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip',
    exact_bboxes: bool = False,
    styles: bool = False,
    max_glyphs: int | None = 262144,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> Layout
```

Return the text of the current version of the page as blocks, lines, and spans, in reading order.

With `chars=True`, every span also lists its characters as
`Char` records: each glyph keeps its complete Unicode mapping,
ligatures included, and each space that pyropdf infers from a gap is a
char with `is_synthetic` set, so that a span's chars join to its
text. A glyph of the page's own content streams names the stream and
the index in `operations` of the operation that showed it, in
`Char.stream` and `Char.operation`, which a second interpretation
of the content finds. Boxes are in display space and span the glyphs' advances and the
font's ascender and descender, or their outlines with
`exact_bboxes=True`. Dehyphenation removes the hyphen from the end
of the line and keeps both lines. `styles=True` also reads the
page's vector rules and sets `Span.is_underlined` and
`Span.is_struck` where a horizontal rule underlines or strikes
out horizontal text, as pymupdf's `TEXT_COLLECT_STYLES` does. The
other options are those of `text`, and `max_size` also bounds
the UTF-8 of the layout's strings.

### `Page.chars`

```python
Page.chars(
    *,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    clipped: bool = False,
    ligatures: bool = True,
    whitespace: bool = True,
    dehyphenate: bool = False,
    unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip',
    exact_bboxes: bool = False,
    styles: bool = False,
    max_glyphs: int | None = 262144,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> Chars
```

Return the chars of the current version of the page as `Chars` columns, in layout order.

The rows are the chars of `layout` with `chars=True` and the
same options, built without a Python object per char: their
`block`, `line`, and `span` columns index that layout, and the
row view builds each `Char` on demand. The options are those
of `layout`.

### `Page.search`

```python
Page.search(
    text: str,
    *,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    quads: bool = False,
    max_hits: int | None = 4096,
    clipped: bool = False,
    ligatures: bool = True,
    whitespace: bool = True,
    dehyphenate: bool = False,
    unmapped: Unmapped = 'skip',
    exact_bboxes: bool = False,
    max_glyphs: int | None = 262144,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> list[Rect] | list[Quad]
```

Search the text of the current version of the page case-insensitively for `text`.

Return one `Rect` per match, or with `quads=True` one
`Quad` per line of each match: a quad follows the baseline,
so that it covers rotated text tightly where a rectangle is
axis-aligned. Search reads the lines of `layout` and finds no
match across lines, except that `dehyphenate=True` joins a
hyphenated word's lines; a match across that join gives one
rectangle that spans both parts, or one quad per line. A space that
pyropdf infers from a gap matches a space of `text`.

`text` is at most 4,096 bytes in UTF-8, or the call raises
`LimitError` with code `search_input_size`. More matches
than `max_hits` raise `LimitError` with code
`search_hit_count` instead of returning some of them;
`max_hits=None` lifts the limit for trusted input. The other
options are those of `layout`.

### `Page.selection`

```python
Page.selection(
    start: Sequence[float],
    end: Sequence[float],
    *,
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    max_glyphs: int | None = 262144,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> str
```

Return the text that a viewer selects by dragging from `start` to `end`.

The selection runs in reading order from the character nearest
`start` to the one nearest `end`, whichever comes first, with the
first and last lines in part and the lines between them whole, as
`text` assembles them, and without a final line break. Both
points are in display space; `clip` limits the characters as
`text` does, and so do the budgets. A page without text
selects `""`.

### `Page.markdown`

```python
Page.markdown(
    *,
    table_strategy: Literal['lines', 'text'] | None = 'lines',
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> str
```

Return the current version of the page as Markdown.

This is `Document.markdown` of this page alone, which infers
heading sizes from this page.

### `Page.tables`

```python
Page.tables(
    *,
    strategy: Literal['lines', 'text'] = 'lines',
    clip: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    max_glyphs: int | None = 262144,
    max_size: int | None = 67108864,
) -> list[Table]
```

Find the tables of the current version of the page from vector rules or aligned text.

The `"lines"` strategy reads the page's stroked rules and thin
filled rectangles. It needs an outer grid of at least two rows and
two columns, and rebuilds rectangular merged cells. It splits a
coarse span of the grid when at least three evenly led text records
occupy the same cells across it.

The `"text"` strategy finds a borderless table only where at least
three consecutive rows have the same number of segments, aligned
column edges, compatible leading, and clear gaps between columns.
Aligned multicolumn prose can pass for a table, so use it where the
page is known to hold tabular data.

`clip` is a display-space rectangle: only the tables whose whole
box lies inside it are returned, and no part of a table is. Each
table carries `TableDiagnostics`. The page's glyphs count
against `max_glyphs` and `max_size` as for `text`.
Exceeding 4,096 vector rules, 4,096 cells per candidate table,
65,536 merged-cell candidates per grid, or 32 text columns raises
`LimitError`, with no partial table results.

### `Page.operations`

```python
Page.operations: Operations
```

The page's content as `Operations`, as hayro reads it.

The content streams of `/Contents` are decoded and joined as the
renderer joins them, each stream of an array followed by one space,
and tokenized with hayro's parser, so the operations are the ones
that rendering interprets. Each operation keeps its bytes, so
`page.operations.to_bytes()` is that content.

Assigning a sequence of `Operation` and `InlineImage`
values writes them as one new Flate-compressed content stream that
replaces `/Contents`, in one transaction, so a stream that other
pages share stays theirs. Operations that a read produced write
their bytes back, so `page.operations = page.operations` keeps
what renders. More than 64 MiB of written content raises
`LimitError` code `content_input_size`.

Reading refuses more than 1,048,576 operations
(`content_operation_count`) and more than 64 MiB of joined content
(`content_stream_size`), besides the decoding limits of
`DocumentLimits`; use `Operations.parse` with
`max_operations=None` on `page.obj["Contents"].read()` for larger
trusted content. The GIL is released while the content is read.

Settable.

## `Pages`

```python
Pages(document: Document)
```

The pages of a document, in order.

Indexing, slicing, and iteration give `Page` handles, which keep
naming their pages through later edits. `new`, `insert`,
`del`, `select`, and `move` each change the page tree in
one transaction.

### `Pages.__len__`

```python
Pages.__len__() -> int
```

Return the number of pages.

### `Pages.labeled`

```python
Pages.labeled(label: str) -> list[int]
```

Return the indexes of the pages whose page label is `label`.

An empty label, or a document without page labels, matches no page.

### `Pages.__getitem__`

```python
Pages.__getitem__(index: int | slice) -> Page | list[Page]
```

Return page `index`, or a list of the pages of a slice.

### `Pages.__iter__`

```python
Pages.__iter__() -> Iterator[Page]
```

Iterate over the pages; a structural edit during the iteration raises `RuntimeError`.

### `Pages.index`

```python
Pages.index(page: object, start: int = 0, stop: int | None = None) -> int
```

Return the index of `page`, in time that does not grow with the page count.

### `Pages.new`

```python
Pages.new(
    size: tuple[float, float] = (595.0, 842.0),
    *,
    index: int | None = None,
) -> Page
```

Add a blank page of `size` points, A4 by default, where `list.insert` would put it.

Without `index` the page goes last. The page has its own MediaBox,
and no rotation or crop of the page tree's root carries over to it.

### `Pages.new_from_image`

```python
Pages.new_from_image(
    source: str | os.PathLike[str] | bytes | bytearray | memoryview | Pixmap,
    *,
    dpi: float | tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    index: int | None = None,
) -> list[Page]
```

Add one page per frame of an image, each the size of its frame at its resolution, in one transaction.

`source` is a path, encoded bytes, or a `Pixmap`. JPEG and
JPEG 2000 data is embedded as it is, without recompression, and PNG
keeps its alpha as a soft mask; each is one frame. Other formats,
such as multi-page TIFF, GIF, or WebP, are read through Pillow when
it is installed, one frame per page, up to 4,096 frames and 256
million pixels in all, from up to 256 MiB of data. A frame's resolution comes from its JFIF
density or Exif resolution, PNG `pHYs`, or Pillow's `dpi`, else
96 dpi, and `dpi`, one number or `(x, y)`,
overrides it. The pages go where `new` puts one, in order, and
are returned.

### `Pages.insert`

```python
Pages.insert(index: int, pages: Page | Iterable[Page])
```

Insert copies of `pages` before `index`, clamped as `list.insert` clamps it, in one transaction.

`pages` is one `Page` or an iterable of pages of one open
document, this one or another. Pages of this document may repeat;
each copy is a new page object that shares the content streams and
resources of its original, with annotations, widgets, and structure
elements of its own. Pages of another document are imported with
what they reach, once each per call; their links to pages imported
with them keep leading there, and their other links within that
document go. Their structure elements join this document's
structure tree, under its single `Document` element when it has
one. The iterable may hold up to the larger of the source's page
count and 4,096 pages.

### `Pages.extend`

```python
Pages.extend(pages: Page | Iterable[Page])
```

Append copies of `pages`, as `insert` at the end inserts them.

### `Pages.select`

```python
Pages.select(indexes: Iterable[int], /)
```

Keep the pages at `indexes`, in that order, and remove the others, in one transaction.

Negative indexes count from the end. A repeated index adds a copy, as
`insert` copies a page. The navigation that leads to a removed
page goes, as for `del`.

### `Pages.move`

```python
Pages.move(index: int, to: int)
```

Move page `index` so that it ends at index `to`, in one transaction.
